title: Commercial Bank Examination Manual, 3000—Capital, Earnings, Liquidity, and Sensitivity to Market Risk
summary: This source is a section of the Federal Reserve's Commercial Bank Examination Manual (Section 3000) covering capital adequacy assessment procedures for bank examiners. It describes regulatory capital components under Regulation Q (Common Equity Tier 1, Additional Tier 1, and Tier 2 capital) and explains the purpose of bank capital in absorbing losses and protecting depositors. The source is a procedural examination manual from November 2020 (effective date), providing supervisory guidance on how examiners assess bank financial condition.
key_points: Section 3000 addresses supervisory assessment of a state member bank's Capital, Earnings, Liquidity, and Sensitivity to market risk (CELS)
Regulation Q (12 CFR Part 217) establishes risk-based capital requirements adopted in 2013 by the Federal Reserve, FDIC, and OCC
The three components of regulatory capital are: (1) Common Equity Tier 1 capital, (2) Additional Tier 1 capital, and (3) Tier 2 capital
Common Equity Tier 1 capital is the highest-quality and most loss-absorbing form of capital, primarily composed of common stock and retained earnings
Capital adequacy triggers the most supervisory action due to the Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) provision of section 38 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act
The effective date of this section is November 2020
